title: Identify a symmetric brominated ketone from sparse NMR
hypothesis: One SMILES from a six-proton singlet and three carbon shifts.
why_hard: Three GPT-5.5 answers terminate normally, but their rank-one structures omit the two bromine atoms in the reference. This proves graph mismatch, not that bromine is uniquely inferable from the supplied input. Screening: Reject this formulation: very sparse input, no formula/mass and an exact hidden identity. A failure to guess unobserved elemental composition is not established genuine difficulty.
next_action: Retain as an identifiability counterexample. A formula-supplied version would be a separately screened task with unknown difficulty.
notes: Independent verifier: A molecular formula or orthogonal measurement is needed before exact identity can be defended; graph equality alone is insufficient. Easy baseline: Enumerate symmetry-compatible skeletons and alternative heteroatom substitutions. New source-screening card, outside the frozen original 100. No local model trial; not submission-ready.
